sections.title: Guided practice
sections.description: Choose the best answer, then read the explanation.

questions.prompt: Last Saturday, we missed the bus, so we ___ to the museum instead.
questions.explanation: “Last Saturday” and the completed sequence require the past simple: went. “Have gone” connects a past action to the present, while “were going” needs an ongoing action or interruption.

questions.prompt: When you were at the station yesterday, ___ you call Mai to tell her about the delay?
questions.explanation: Use Did + base verb for a finished past action: “Did you call…?” “Were” would need an -ing form, and “Have” does not fit with the finished-time marker “yesterday”.

questions.prompt: Although she checked her phone twice last night, she did not ___ the email until this morning.
questions.explanation: After did not, use the base form: receive. The time phrase “last night” makes the negative action a finished past event.

questions.prompt: After their flight landed last night, they ___ at the hotel at 9 p.m. and checked in immediately.
questions.explanation: The arrival is the next completed event after the flight landed, so arrived is the natural past-simple choice. “Had arrived” would need a later past reference point; “were arriving” describes an action in progress.

questions.prompt: Yesterday afternoon, I needed a bag for work, so I ___ one at the market.
questions.explanation: “Yesterday afternoon” and “so” describe one finished event, so use bought, the past form of buy. “Have bought” does not normally go with a finished past time, and “was buying” needs an interrupted or ongoing context.

questions.prompt: We were lost and becoming worried. ___, a stranger stopped and helped us find the station.
questions.explanation: Fortunately signals a positive result after a problem. However introduces contrast, and meanwhile introduces a separate action happening at the same time.

tip.title: Use the clue
tip.text: Look for time expressions, the subject, and words before or after the gap before choosing.

sections.title: Listening: A Memorable Saturday
sections.description: Listen to the story and follow the sequence of events.

audio.transcript: Last Saturday, I planned to meet my cousin at the city museum. I left home at nine, but the bus was twenty minutes late. When I arrived, my cousin was waiting outside with two tickets. First, we visited an exhibition about space travel. Then we had lunch in the museum café. In the afternoon, it started raining, so we decided not to walk in the park. Instead, we watched a film near the station. I got home at seven, tired but very happy.

gistQuestions.explanation: The speaker tells the story of a day at the museum and cinema.

detailQuestions.prompt: Why did the speaker arrive late?
detailQuestions.explanation: The bus was twenty minutes late. Read the complete context before rejecting the other options.

detailQuestions.prompt: What did they do after it started raining?
detailQuestions.explanation: They changed their plan and watched a film.

tip.title: Listening Tip
tip.text: Notice sequence markers such as first, then, in the afternoon and instead.

sections.title: Build a spoken answer
sections.description: Answer each question aloud. Aim for a clear answer plus one reason or detail.
questions: What did you do last weekend?
When did something unexpected happen to you?
sections.sampleAnswer: Last weekend, I visited my grandparents. We cooked lunch and talked for hours. On Sunday, I missed my bus, but fortunately my uncle drove me home.

tip.title: Speak in layers
tip.text: Start with a direct answer, add a reason, then give one example or detail.

sections.title: Independent writing
sections.description: Tell a friend about a memorable weekend.

prompt.situation: Explain where you went, what happened, and how you felt.
prompt.referenceAnswer: Last weekend, I visited my grandparents. We cooked lunch and talked for hours. On Sunday, I missed my bus, but fortunately my uncle drove me home.

tip.title: Final check
tip.text: Check verb forms, word order, spelling, and whether every sentence helps answer the task.
